Surah al-Qalam (The Pen) — Makkan, and its verses number fifty-two.

﴿Nun.﴾ One of the disjointed letters of the alphabet (huruf al-hijaʾ); God alone knows what He intends by it.

﴿By the pen,﴾ with which He wrote all created things on the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

﴿And by what they inscribe,﴾ that is, the angels, [inscribing] what is good and righteous.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 68 (al-Qalam), verse 2:

﴿You are not﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾. That is, madness has been removed from you by reason of your Lord's bestowing upon you prophethood and other favours. This is a refutation of their saying that he is mad.
And surely for you is a reward never cut off. That is, a reward not interrupted.

Khuluq (Ḥuluq) - dīn

Note on the rendering: the Arabic gloss here is "dīn," which in this context means "religion/way of life," and "khuluq" is the Qur'anic word being glossed, so I have kept both as transliterated terms.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 68, verse 6:

﴿Which of you is the afflicted one?﴾ *Maṣdar* (verbal noun, the infinitive form) like *al-maʿqūl* (the reasoned, i.e., reason itself), meaning *al-futūn*, which here means *al-junūn* (madness). I.e., *abika* (is it with you) *am bihim* (or with them)?

Your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are guided. [Qur'an 68:7]

Note: this translation covers the verse and the Jalalayn gloss on it, which reads that "a'lam" here carries the sense of "knowing" ('alim).

﴿They wish﴾ meaning they desire (tamannaw), ﴿that﴾ (law) is a masdariyya (a particle that turns the following verb into a verbal noun, here "that"), ﴿you would be lenient﴾ (tudhin) meaning you would soften toward them, ﴿and they would be lenient﴾ (fayudhinun) meaning they would soften toward you. It is conjoined (ma'tuf) to tudhin. And if the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni), understood from wadda, is taken to be a word supposed before it after the fa', namely hum (they), then [the meaning is as stated].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 10:

﴿And do not obey every ˹habitual˺ swearer, ˹and˺ contemptible﴾ — كَثِير الحَلِف بِالباطِلِ: one who often swears falsely; ﴿مَهِين﴾: despicable (حَقِير), base.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿هَمّاز﴾ = ﴿hammaz﴾... The passage is the Jalalayn gloss on 68:11. I should translate faithfully, keep ﴿ ﴾ markers, translate meaning inside them, transliterate technical terms with glosses on first appearance.

﴿Hammaz﴾, one who finds fault and defames, i.e., one who backbites (mughtab); ﴿mashsha'in bi-namim﴾, one who goes about carrying words among people in order to sow discord between them.

Wait: the instructions say keep ﴿ ﴾ markers and translate meaning inside them plainly. So: ﴿a constant slanderer﴾ ... Let me produce final.

﴿A constant slanderer﴾, i.e., one who finds fault (ʿayyāb), that is, one who backbites (mughtāb); ﴿going about with malicious gossip﴾, i.e., one who carries words between people in order to cause corruption among them.

Verse 12 of Surah al-Qalam (68), as explained in Tafsir al-Jalalayn:

﴿Withholder of the good﴾ stingy with his wealth regarding the rights (due from it). ﴿Transgressor﴾ oppressive. ﴿Sinful﴾ committing sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 13:

﴿Utull﴾ harsh, coarse, violent (ghaliz jaf); ﴿after that, zanim﴾: he was called (a zanim) among the Quraysh, and he was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, whose father claimed him eighteen years after his birth. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "We know of no one whom Allah described with such defects as He described him, and He attached to him a disgrace that never leaves him." The adverbial phrase "after that" (al-zarf) is connected to zanim, which precedes it.
i.e., because he possessed wealth and sons. This [phrase] is connected to what is indicated by that (the preceding words).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 15:

﴿When Our verses are recited to him﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿he says: "They are the fables of the ancients"﴾, i.e., he denied them because of Our favor upon him by what has been mentioned. And in one qira'a (a variant recitation), the word أأَنْ is read with two hamzas, both with fatha.
﴿We will brand him upon the snout.﴾ We will place a mark on his nose by which he will be disgraced for as long as he lives. So his nose was slashed with a sword on the Day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, We have tested them⁠﴾ We tested the people of Makkah with famine and hunger. ﴿as We tested the companions of the garden⁠﴾ i.e., the owners of the orchard, ﴿when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit⁠﴾ cut off its produce, ﴿in the morning⁠﴾ at the time of dawn, so that the needy would not notice them and would not be given any of it, which their father used to give to them as charity from it.
**﴿And they did not make exception⦆** in their oath by the will of Allah, the Exalted. The clause is a new sentence (mustaʾnafah), meaning: and that was their practice.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah al-Qalam (68), verse 19:

﴿Then there swept over it a visitation from your Lord﴾ a fire that burned it during the night.
﴿So it became like the darkest night﴾ (كاللَّيْلِ الشَّدِيد الظُّلْمَة), i.e., black (أيْ سَوْداء).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 22:

﴿That go early to your tilth﴾ (ghallatakum), an explanation of "they called out" (litanadaw); or "an" is a verbal particle (masdariyya), meaning "with that" (bi-an). ﴿If you are going to harvest﴾ (murīdīna al-qat'), meaning intending to cut. The answer to the condition is indicated by what precedes it.
﴿So they set off, whispering to one another﴾ — yatasarrurun, i.e. speaking together in low voices.

﴿That no needy person shall enter it upon you today.﴾

Its being an explanation (*tafsir*) of what precedes it, or *an* being a verbal particle (*masdariyyah*), meaning "with that," i.e., "by that."

And they set out early, [determined] upon withholding (from the poor), [thinking] themselves able to do so.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿وَغَدَوْا عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ ۝ قَادِرِينَ﴾ — "And they set out early in the morning, determined [to withhold], thinking themselves able [to do it]."

﴿When they saw it﴾ black and burnt, ﴿they said, "We have surely gone astray"﴾ from it, i.e., this is not it. Then they said, once they recognised it: "Indeed we are deprived" (mahrumun), i.e., deprived of its fruit.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 27:

﴿Nay, we are deprived﴾ of its fruit by our having withheld it from the poor.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 28:

﴿Said the most moderate of them﴾ (khayrahum, i.e. the best of them) ﴿Did I not tell you: "Why not"﴾ (halla, i.e. "why do you not") ﴿glorify﴾ God, repenting.
﴿They said, "Glory be to our Lord; indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ [They were wrongdoers] by withholding the poor their due.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 31:

﴿They said: "O﴾ (for alerting) ﴿woe to us!﴾ (i.e., our destruction)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 32:

﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it﴾, with the verb read with doubled or single letter (tashdid and takhfif), ﴿for we turn to our Lord in longing﴾, so that He may accept our repentance and return to us something better than our garden. It is narrated that they were given in exchange something better than it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 33:

﴿Thus﴾ i.e., like this punishment for these people, ﴿is the punishment﴾ for whoever opposes Our command, from the disbelievers of Makkah and others, ﴿and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾ its punishment; they would not have opposed Our command. And it was revealed when they said: "If we are resurrected, we will be given something better than you."
﴿Shall We then treat the submitters like the criminals?﴾ i.e., following them in the gift (of reward).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 36:

﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ This corrupt judgment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 37:

﴿Am﴾ meaning: rather (bal), and the hamza (interrogative) ... ﴿Lakum kitab﴾ (Or do you have a Book) sent down ﴿fihi tadrusun﴾ (in which you study), meaning: you read.

﷽ — no, I'll translate directly.

Translation:

﴿Indeed, for you therein is what you choose.﴾ Yakhtarun (you choose).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 39:

﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, extending to the Day of Resurrection﴾ ʿUhūd (covenants), wathiqa (firm), ﴿extending to the Day of Resurrection﴾ muta‘alliq (connected) in meaning with ʿalaynā (upon Us). In this statement there is the meaning of an oath, i.e., "We have sworn to you," and its answer is ﴿that yours is whatever you judge﴾ by it for yourselves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 40:

﴿Ask them, which of them stands surety for that﴾, the judgment they pass for themselves, namely that they will be given better than the believers in the Hereafter. ﴿Surety﴾: a guarantor for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have partners﴾, i.e., with them, ﴿who agree with them in this claim and stand surety for it on their behalf?﴾ If that is so, ﴿then let them bring their partners﴾ who stand surety for them in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 42:

﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾ — this is an expression for the severity of the matter on the Day of Resurrection, for reckoning and recompense. It is said: "The war uncovered its shin," meaning when the matter in it became intense. ﴿And they will be called to prostration﴾ — as a test of their faith. ﴿But they will not be able to﴾ — their backs will become one single level plane (ṭabaqan wāḥidan).

﴿Humbled﴾ (*khāshi'a*) is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier, a clause describing the state of the subject at the time of the action) referring back to the pronoun in ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ (*yad'ūna*, "they are called"). Its meaning is: abased, ﴿their eyes﴾ (*abṣāruhum*) lowered, not lifting them. ﴿Humiliation covers them﴾ (*tarhaquhum*): it overwhelms them (*taghshāhum*), ﴿dhilla﴾ (*dhilla*), that is, disgrace. ﴿And they had been called﴾ (*wa-qad kānū yud'awna*) in the world ﴿to prostration﴾ (*ilā al-sujūd*) ﴿while they were sound﴾ (*wa-hum sālimūn*), that is, healthy and able, ﴿so they would not comply with it﴾ (*fa-lā ya'tūna bihi*), by not praying (*bi-an lā yuṣallū*).
﴿So leave Me﴾ to Me, ﴿and [leave] those who deny this discourse﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿We will draw them on gradually﴾ We will seize them little by little.
[Qur'an 68:45] "And I give them respite." (ʾUmlī lahum) — give them time/leave them be. "Indeed, My plan is firm." (inna kaydī matīn) — strong, unbearable, not to be withstood.
Or (rather) do you ask them for a wage (for conveying the message), so that they are burdened with debt (from what they would have to pay you) and so do not believe because of that?
﴿Am ʿindahumu al-ghayb﴾ (Or do they have the unseen?), i.e., the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which the unseen is recorded. ﴿Fa-hum yaktubun﴾ (so they write down from it) what they say.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 48:

﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾ concerning them, as He wills. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ in hastiness and impatience, and he is Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him. ﴿When he called out﴾ he called upon his Lord, ﴿while he was suppressed﴾ full of grief, in the belly of the fish.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 49:

﴿Had it not been that a favour from his Lord had overtaken him﴾ — lawlā an adrakahu (had it not been that it reached him), ﴿a favour﴾ — raḥma (mercy), ﴿from his Lord﴾, ﴿he would have been cast forth﴾ — from the belly of the fish, ﴿onto the barren land﴾ — onto the open ground, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ — but he was shown mercy, so he was cast forth not blameworthy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 50:

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾ with prophethood, ﴿and made him of the righteous﴾, i.e., of the prophets.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 68, verse 51:

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieved would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾ (pronounced with a damma on the yā' and with a fatḥa on it, i.e., "yuzliqūnaka" and "yazlaqūnaka") ﴿when they hear the Reminder﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿and they say, "Indeed, he is a madman!"﴾ — out of envy — ﴿on account of the Qur'an that he has brought.﴾ They look at you with an intense gaze, almost as if it would throw you down and make you fall from your place.

Verse 52 is "And it is not but a reminder to the worlds," and the commentary reads:

﴿And it is not﴾ i.e., the Qur'an ﴿but a reminder﴾ an admonition ﴿to the worlds﴾ the jinn and mankind, [and it] does not arise from a cause of madness.
